gaps.text: In-line measurement of Product temperature with temperature sensor

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (NIR and MIR must look at the same product volume, so a combined or co-located probe head is needed; alternating probes cannot guarantee the same spot. The two methods acquire at different rates, so their data must be aligned to a common time step, and each method keeps its own calibration and diagnostics. Start with one model per method, then test a concatenated fusion with block scaling, and keep it only if it beats the best single method on held-out runs.)
No supplied source states an achievable fiber-optic link length for a mid-infrared probe, so the distance from instrument to probe for an MIR ATR option is an open question.
No supplied source covers dairy cleaning, fouling or sanitation requirements at an in-line probe.

items.finding: Temperature sensitivity of OH bands in aqueous solutions is a severe drawback for NIR and MIR, making tempered sample holders necessary.
items.how_it_applies: For an in-line NIR concept on milk, product temperature may affect spectra, so include temperature measurement or control and test temperature variation.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is a review of biopharmaceutical downstream processing, not dairy; tempered sample holders are not the same as an in-line product temperature sensor.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E02 ¶12

items.finding: In rice authentication, MIR alone gave better classification accuracy than NIR, while a SPORT-based multiblock fusion of MIR and NIR improved use of spectral variability and robustness.
items.how_it_applies: This supports starting with one model per method and then testing a concatenated fusion with block scaling, keeping it only if it beats the best single method on held-out runs.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The study is on rice authentication, abstract only, and likely laboratory-based; the matrix, application, and classification task differ from an opaque dairy stream.

citation.quote: When analysed individually, MIR showed better predictive performance than NIR in terms of classification accuracy. The SPORT-based multiblock approach, integrating complementary MIR and NIR information, improved the exploitation of spectral variability and provided a more robust framework for modelling complex authenticity patterns.
citation.label: E04 ¶1

items.finding: PAT integration addresses challenges including compatibility of PAT tools with data fusion.
items.how_it_applies: This suggests data fusion is a recognized area, but compatibility and data-treatment challenges should be tested for the chosen NIR/MIR setup.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is a pharmaceutical PAT abstract, not dairy-specific, and does not address co-located NIR/MIR probes or time alignment.

citation.quote: The integration of PAT in pharmaceutical processes not only ensures product quality, consistency, and regulatory compliance but also addresses challenges related to process implementation, data treatment algorithms, and the compatibility of PAT tools with data fusion [ 51 , 83 ].
citation.label: E05 ¶1

items.finding: Contamination of the probe window during processing may make accurate measurement not possible.
items.how_it_applies: For an in-line probe, fouling or contamination of the optical window is a risk to monitor and include in cleaning and validation planning.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source describes a pharmaceutical process with a binder, not dairy; it does not cover dairy cleaning or sanitation requirements.

citation.quote: However, an accurate measurement may not be possible because of contamination of the probe window due to the addition of a binder during the process, which is a disadvantage.
citation.label: E03 ¶27
